items.name: Peppa Pig
clues: Cheeky, a bit bossy and very sure of herself. She thinks she knows best.
Pre-school children, and parents who know every episode by heart.
A British cartoon, first shown on TV in 2004.
Pink, round and drawn very simply, with both eyes on the same side of her head.
In 2021 parents in the USA said their children had started speaking with a British accent after watching her.
Her favourite thing is jumping in muddy puddles. In German, her surname is “Wutz”.

items.name: Hello Kitty
clues: Sweet, kind and quiet. Fans say she never needs to say anything.
Children, teenagers and adult collectors all over the world.
A Japanese company created her in 1974. A year later, the first product was a small plastic purse for coins.
White, with a red bow by her left ear, and no mouth.
Although she comes from Japan, her official story says she was born near London.
Her name is a friendly English greeting plus a word for a young cat.

items.name: Paddington
clues: Polite, curious and always getting into trouble without meaning to.
Children, parents, and in 2022 even the Queen, who had tea with him on TV.
His first book came out in London in 1958.
A duffel coat, an old hat and a label round his neck that says “Please look after this bear. Thank you.”
His writer first wanted him to come from Africa, but was told there were no bears there. So he comes from Peru.
He is named after a big railway station in London.

items.name: The Moomins
clues: Gentle, thoughtful and a little bit sad sometimes. Everyone is welcome in their house.
Children, but also adults who buy the mugs and the tote bags.
A Finnish artist who wrote in Swedish published the first book about them in 1945.
White, round and soft, with big snouts. Some people think they look like small hippos.
They are hugely popular in Japan, where a theme park about them opened near Tokyo in 2019.
A family of trolls who live in a valley named after them. In German, they are the Mumins.

items.name: Miffy
clues: Simple, calm and friendly. Nothing about her is ever complicated.
Very small children, and lots of designers who love her style.
A Dutch artist from Utrecht drew her for the first time in 1955.
A few thick black lines and a small number of bright colours. Her mouth is a little cross, and she always looks straight at you.
There is a museum just for her in her home city in the Netherlands.
A little white rabbit. In Dutch she is Nijntje, from the word for “little rabbit”.

items.name: Pippi Longstocking
clues: Wild, funny and completely free. She doesn’t follow anyone’s rules.
Children who want to be brave, and adults who remember wanting to be brave.
A Swedish writer published her first book about her in 1945.
Red hair in two plaits that stick out sideways, freckles and stockings that don’t match.
She is the strongest girl in the world and can lift her own horse. In the German TV theme song, she sings that two times three makes four.
Her surname in English describes her very long socks. In German, she is Langstrumpf.
